title: Neuro De-Armoring Cards, 27 November (2): the herbs warning with 73a, and the Cognitive Warning, for you to teach me

items.title: Lion's mane and ashwagandha with 73a: nine tries, my best High then Medium
items.where: A Complete Guide to Bio-De-Armoring, P9
items.your_version: I'm not advising lion's mane or ashwagandha, even though they're popular herbs for focus and stress, because some people report anhedonia (no joy or desire) and sexual dysfunction long after they stop taking them. Post-ashwa and post-lion's mane syndrome are rare, but we know about this phenomenon already from SSRIs and finasteride users, so if you're already on either herb, I'd quit it as soon as you notice any of that.

items.title: The Cognitive Warning and the paragraph after it: High by themselves, one Medium window in the section
items.where: A Complete Guide to Bio-De-Armoring, P7
items.your_version:
As you de-armor, you will feel naked and exposed, and you will assume everyone can see your anxiety, which they mostly can't. Nicholas Epley, Mindwise, calls this the "Illusion of Transparency."

On top of that, you'll tend to think people are judging you, when really they're mostly just thinking about themselves. That's because when your brain is armored up, you project the nonsensical threat you feel onto others. So during this protocol, do not trust your social intuition: assume you are misreading every room, at least until your heart rate is back down to your usual resting rate, and under 90 BPM, since a racing heart means your reasoning brain is offline (see the "Metabolic Red Line" below).
